market_summary: Global equity markets are navigating mixed signals as investors weigh geopolitical tensions—particularly Trump's Iran comments and Middle East uncertainty—against ongoing AI infrastructure investment by major US tech firms. Oil prices have risen amid regional tensions. Singapore banks reported solid Q2 earnings with wealth management offsetting margin compression, while UOB outlined a major private banking expansion. In the US, large-cap tech companies face scrutiny on premium product pricing and regulatory probes, though they continue infrastructure buildouts. A broad theme: interest rate normalization is shifting focus toward fee income and operational efficiency.

items.headline: DBS Group Q2 earnings rise 9% YoY with record quarterly income; Phillip Securities raises target to SGD 85
items.summary: DBS posted record Q2 2026 net profit of SGD 3.1 billion, up 9.0% year-over-year and 5.0% quarter-over-quarter, with total income reaching SGD 6.1 billion. Phillip Securities raised its target price to SGD 85 from SGD 79, citing capital strength and expected sustainable ROE of 16.7%.

items.headline: UOB earmarks SGD 800 million for five-year private banking expansion
items.summary: United Overseas Bank plans to add 50 relationship managers annually and invest SGD 800 million (USD 627 million) over five years to accelerate private bank growth, including opening a Hong Kong booking center.

items.headline: UOB Q1 net profit up 0.6% YoY to SGD 505 million as Singapore banks rise
items.summary: UOB reported Q1 net profit of SGD 505 million, up 0.6% year-over-year from SGD 502 million, as Singapore's three major banks all advanced in trading.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines initiates share buyback, purchases 500,000 shares for SGD 3.3 million
items.summary: Singapore Airlines started buying back its shares on September 16, 2026, purchasing 500,000 shares for SGD 3.3 million (USD 2.6 million) at SGD 6.53-6.58 per share, representing 0.02% of issued shares.

items.headline: Singapore Airlines fleet expands to 153 aircraft; adds new 737 MAX and returns A350 to service
items.summary: Singapore Airlines now has 153 passenger aircraft in service, its largest fleet since before the pandemic, with recent additions including one new 737 MAX delivery and return of repaired A350 after landing mishap.

items.headline: Apple introduces foldable iPhone under new CEO Ternus; premium strategy tested beyond early adopters
items.summary: Apple opened the Ternus era with a foldable iPhone launch, testing whether the premium device strategy can attract customers beyond early adopters as competition intensifies in the smartphone market.

items.headline: Apple faces deeper iPhone probe in India; software warranty becomes key issue
items.summary: Apple is undergoing a more extensive regulatory investigation in India regarding iPhones, with software warranty becoming a central focus of the inquiry.

items.headline: Microsoft plans vast data center expansion to justify Azure infrastructure investment
items.summary: Microsoft reportedly plans a major data center expansion, raising questions about whether the infrastructure investments can be justified through Azure service growth and AI capabilities.

items.headline: Elon Musk gives Nvidia investors more good news as stock attracts analyst attention
items.summary: Elon Musk made comments supporting Nvidia that boosted investor sentiment, with analysts continuing to evaluate whether the stock remains a solid investment.

items.headline: Amazon pauses cargo carrier operations after fatal crash; air network faces disruption risk
items.summary: Amazon suspended operations of a cargo carrier following a fatal crash, raising questions about the airline's ability to absorb the operational disruption.

items.headline: Amazon calls for AI safeguards without slowdown; AWS positioned to benefit
items.summary: Amazon advocated for artificial intelligence safeguards that don't impede industry progress, positioning AWS to capitalize on responsible AI development.

items.headline: Amazon partners with Prysmian and Rio Tinto for low-carbon data center cables
items.summary: Amazon secured partnerships with Prysmian and Rio Tinto for low-carbon cables supporting its data center expansion, aligning infrastructure with sustainability goals.

items.headline: Dow Jones futures fall, oil prices rise amid Trump Iran comments; Tesla eyes buy points
items.summary: Dow Jones futures declined and oil prices rose following Trump's comments on Iran, with Tesla and Micron among stocks identified as potentially attracting buyers at current levels.
